Standardise survey records to the svyexpo schema

Source: R/ingest.R
svy_standardize.Rd

Renames user-specified columns to the standard names in svy_schema(), removes records with missing coordinates and returns an sf POINT object. Records at (0, 0) are treated as missing because DHS uses this value for clusters without GPS data.

Usage

svy_standardize(
  data,
  id,
  cluster,
  lon,
  lat,
  date = NULL,
  weight = NULL,
  strata = NULL,
  urban = NULL,
  crs = 4326
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per survey record.

id, cluster, lon, lat

Names of the columns holding the record identifier, cluster identifier, longitude and latitude.

date, weight, strata, urban

Optional column names for interview date, sampling weight, stratum and urban/rural status. urban may be logical, "U"/"R", "urban"/"rural", or DHS-coded 1 (urban) / 2 (rural).

crs

Coordinate reference system of lon/lat. Defaults to WGS84.

Value

An sf object with standard columns first, followed by all other columns of data. Original columns whose names clash with a standard name are kept with an orig_ prefix.

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  hhid = c("a", "b", "c"), clust = c(1, 1, 2),
  x = c(-0.20, -0.21, 0), y = c(5.60, 5.61, 0),
  stunted = c(0, 1, 0), res = c("U", "U", "R")
)
svy_standardize(df, id = "hhid", cluster = "clust", lon = "x", lat = "y",
                urban = "res")
#> Warning: Dropped 1 record with missing or (0, 0) coordinates.
#> Simple feature collection with 2 features and 6 fields
#> Geometry type: POINT
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: -0.21 ymin: 5.6 xmax: -0.2 ymax: 5.61
#> Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84
#>   id cluster   lon  lat urban stunted           geometry
#> 1  a       1 -0.20 5.60  TRUE       0   POINT (-0.2 5.6)
#> 2  b       1 -0.21 5.61  TRUE       1 POINT (-0.21 5.61)
